text: EU imposes anti-dumping duty on cold-rolled steel from Việt Nam

HÀ NỘI - The EU has imposed a 16 per cent anti-dumping duty on certain cold-rolled steel products originating from five countries and territories including Việt Nam, in a move that could affect the competitiveness of Vietnamese exporters in the European market.

The Ministry of Industry and Trade said on November 17 that the European Commission (EC) issued a decision on November 13 imposing anti-dumping duties on certain flat-rolled products of cold-rolled iron or non-alloy steel and other alloy steel originating from India, Japan, Taiwan (China), Türkiye and Việt Nam.
Under the decision, starting on November 17, products originating in Việt Nam are subject to a 16 per cent anti-dumping duty.
Rates for other economies are 9.5 per cent for India, 27.9 per cent for Japan, between 20.7 per cent and 27 per cent for Taiwan (China), and between 3 per cent and 7.8 per cent for Türkiye.
The EC concluded that imports from the countries and territories covered by the investigation had been dumped and had caused injury to the EU industry manufacturing similar products.
Launched on September 18, 2025, the investigation followed a complaint filed by the European Steel Association.
The Việt Nam Trade Office in Belgium said that the measure could directly affect the competitiveness and export performance of Vietnamese cold-rolled steel producers in the EU market.
The trade office urged Vietnamese steel exporters to review the product scope, applicable duty rates and import documentation requirements under the regulation.
Firms have also been encouraged to maintain coordination with relevant authorities to protect their legitimate rights and interests during the implementation of the trade defence measures. - VNS
